title: Ops + PM 1:1 prep — priorities & quick asks
content:
Context: quick prep notes for my 1:1 with Omar (eng lead) — focus on short blockers that need decisions (rate limiting strategy for hosted API), Dedicated capacity forecast for Q2, and the Private onboarding checklist for the Acme pilot. Keep this to 20–30m: status, 3 asks, and next actions.

Meeting goals (top level):
- Align on immediate decisions that unblock product launches (2–3 day turnaround if possible).
- Confirm owner + ETA for Dedicated capacity sizing doc and provisioning runbook.
- Agree on Private onboarding gating list items we can remove or automate.

Agenda (20 min):
1) Quick sync (2m): what changed since last week — capacity alert + one regression on streaming.
2) API rate-limit defaults (6m) — decision needed: tighten burst vs per-second baseline for free-tier to avoid noisy neighbors.
3) Dedicated capacity forecast (6m) — confirm numbers for next commit, how much headroom to reserve for canary rollouts.
4) Private deployment onboarding (4m) — blocker list and temporary mitigation.
5) Actions & ownership (2m).

Key background notes (keep handy):
- Observability: 03/08 spike in free-tier streaming requests -> transient 95th p95 token latency increase. Related to continuous batching heuristics failing for tiny payloads (INF-2432).
- Current hosted rate-limit: 10 req/s burst 100 per minute for free. Prod customers on dedicated have soft-limits controlled by quota service.
- Dedicated capacity: finance asked for updated forecast by Mar 20 to finalize reserved contract numbers. We can propose 10% bump over current steady-state to cover rollouts.
- Private onboarding: Acme pilot needs SSO + HSM integration + audit logs export. SSO mostly done; HSM still manual (ticket INF-2589).

Decisions I'm asking for in 1:1: (be explicit)
- D1: Should we reduce free-tier burst from 100/min -> 40/min to reduce noisy neighbor risk, or add jittering in batching to smooth spikes? (preferred: quick config -- reduce burst; longer term: batching fix)
- D2: Approve provisional Dedicated buffer of +10% for Q2 commit to be used only for canaries and emergency spillover. (If no, we need a fallback policy: route to cheaper GPU pool w/ higher latency)
- D3: Prioritize automation for HSM onboarding (INF-2589) as P1 for Private pilot. Request estimate: dev + SRE effort in dev days.

Open questions to surface:
- Q1: How risky is dropping the free-tier burst now vs. expected customer impact? Any customers we should whitelist?
- Q2: Who will own the rollback plan if the reduced burst causes legitimate errors? (suggest: Console routing team owns monitoring + auto-fallback)
- Q3: For Dedicated buffer, can we implement a strict cutover schedule tied to billing cycle to avoid contract exposure?

Notes / prompts I'll use live:
- "Omar — if we don't tighten free-tier burst this week we risk repeated p95 spikes that distort our autoscaling signals and drive up cost. We can whitelist the top 5 integrations for a week. Thoughts?"
- "For Dedicated: finance wants numbers. If we go +10% buffer we get safe canaries and avoid forced throttles; do you see any infra objections?"

Immediate TODOs / follow-ups (post-meeting):
- A1 (Priya) create short proposal doc with config delta matrix for free-tier (3 options) and impact analysis — target Mar 13. Link to INF ticket.
- A2 (Omar) quick estimate for HSM automation (INF-2589) — rough dev + SRE days by Mar 15.
- A3 (Kai) run a query to list top 20 free-tier customers by average qps and flag for potential whitelist — due Mar 12.
- A4 (SRE) add alert for "batching-undersize" regressions to triage channel — owner: SRE oncall.
- A5 (Priya + Omar) sync with finance and legal re: Dedicated buffer proposal — set meeting Mar 17 if decision made.

Risk notes (to mention briefly):
- Rate limiting too aggressive -> developer frustration and increased support tickets. Need a temporary support playbook.
- Dedicated buffer increases committed spend; must be justified vs. expected revenue from enterprise pilots.
- HSM manual steps create onboarding delays and audit risk for Acme.

Snippets to copy into JIRA/PRs: 
- "Proposal: temporarily reduce free-tier burst quota from 100/min to 40/min and monitor p95 latency for 72h. Whitelist top N integrations to minimize impact. Rollback plan: revert config and notify users via status page if error rate > 1%."
- "Dedicated buffer request: provision +10% reserved GPU minutes for Q2 to support canary rollouts and emergency capacity; will be reconciled at month-end. Owner: product + infra lead."

Misc quick links I might paste in meeting:
- Perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood-inference.internal/p/perf?view=free-tier
- INF-2432 (batching/regression): https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-2432
- HSM onboarding ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-2589
- PR for batching fix (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/612

Personal notes / voice: keep this short — focus on decisions not engineering design. If Omar pushes back on priority, escalate HSM automation as critical for pilot revenue.

Follow-up format I’ll send after meeting (template):
- Decisions made: D1 = X, D2 = Y, D3 = Z
- Action owners + dates: A1 / A2 / A3 ...
- Risks called out + mitigation steps
- Next sync (if needed) time/date

End of scratch.

(Will convert to tidy email after the 1:1 if decisions confirmed.)
